name: RxDB
tagline: Reactive local-first NoSQL database for JavaScript with pluggable storage and replication.
description: RxDB is a TypeScript document database that runs in browsers, React Native, Electron, Capacitor and Node, with every query exposed as an observable so UIs update automatically. Storage is pluggable (IndexedDB, OPFS, SQLite, memory and more) and replication plugins sync with CouchDB, GraphQL, HTTP endpoints, Firestore, Supabase, NATS or WebRTC peers. It is one of the most actively maintained JavaScript local-first options. The catch is that the fastest storage engines and some plugins are paid premium add-ons, and its JSON-schema document model is not a fit for relational queries.

pricing.notes: Core is free; premium plugins (OPFS, SQLite, sharding and other storages) need a paid license.

scale.notes: Client-side store; practical sizes are bounded by device storage and chosen backend.

strengths: Every query is an observable, so UI state stays in sync with stored data
Swappable storage engines from IndexedDB to OPFS and SQLite
Replication plugins for many backends, including peer-to-peer WebRTC
Field-level encryption and key compression plugins
Very active development with frequent releases
weaknesses: Best-performing storages and some features are paid
No joins; relational data must be denormalised or stitched in code
Large plugin surface makes configuration and bundle size easy to get wrong
useCases: React Native and Capacitor apps with background sync
Electron apps needing local reactive storage
Multi-tab browser apps sharing one database
notIdealFor: Relational data models with heavy joins
Projects that cannot use paid plugins but need top performance
